recent_trades.summary: Add to EOG from 7.5% to 9% as IEA flags deepening oil supply shortfall and Saudi Red Sea exports go dark.
recent_trades.reasoning: EOG is a direct upstream oil producer with high sensitivity to crude prices. Current supply-side catalysts are concrete: IEA says global 2026 oil supply shortfall will deepen because Hormuz reopening remains elusive, and Saudi Red Sea oil exports have gone dark on increasing Houthi attack threats. This supports higher realized oil prices and EOG cash flows. Position sizing from 7.5% to 9% keeps it within single-name limits while making it a meaningful overweight to the strongest current theme.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to LLY on fresh rating upgrade and strong technical breakout in healthcare.
recent_trades.reasoning: LLY up over 1% today with positive momentum; new SeekingAlpha analysis highlights underestimated Retatrutide potential (weight-loss drug) improving risk/reward, plus confirmed technical breakout. Increasing from ~10.3% to 12% aligns with sector strength while staying under single-name limit.

recent_trades.summary: Adding to EOG position on fresh geopolitical energy tailwinds: Saudi Red Sea exports going dark and Hormuz closure risk deepening supply shortfall per IEA.
recent_trades.reasoning: EOG was initiated yesterday on a SeekingAlpha upgrade. Today's macro headlines are significantly more bullish for energy: (1) IEA warns 2026 global oil supply shortfall deepening as Hormuz reopening remains elusive, (2) Saudi Red Sea oil exports going dark due to Houthi attack threats, (3) Iran nuclear deal showing no progress. These are concrete new geopolitical catalysts that increase the probability of sustained elevated oil prices. EOG as a high-quality E&P with strong dividend growth (noted in SA's top 50 dividend growth stocks) is well-positioned. COP also has a Susquehanna PT raise to $161. Adding to EOG from 5% to 8% is warranted. The position is only down -0.43% so no reversal concerns.

recent_trades.summary: Add to EOG from 6.5% to 7.5% on escalating oil supply disruptions.
